applies_to: Guidewire PolicyCenter 10.x / Guidewire Cloud / earlier on-premise
info_to_collect: Policy, term, audit job number and audit type (final, interim, revision, non-compliant)
Each GL exposure: class code, location/state, basis type (payroll, sales, area, units), estimated and audited basis
Whether Products-Completed Operations applies; limits (each occurrence / aggregate)
Expected premium and direction vs premium shown
Mid-term changes (class added/removed, location or limit change) and dates; keyed by auditor or automation; screenshots
title: GL audit premium moves the wrong way against the reported basis, or a revised audit cannot correct it
symptoms: GL audit premium decreases when payroll or sales increase (or the reverse)
GL audit premium too high; a revised audit cannot correct it
cause: GL premium per exposure = (basis / divisor) x rate x ILF x modifiers, rated separately for Premises/Operations and Products-Completed Operations, then minimums; audit premium = audited premium minus premium charged. Inversions usually mean the estimated basis was rated on a slice, the wrong divisor or basis type was used, the delta sign is wrong, a minimum premium hid the change, or a revision used the wrong based-on period.
diagnosis: Hold the audit invoice in Billing
Run the direction test: higher audited basis must mean higher premium on that exposure unless a minimum applies
Recompute per exposure and slice: (basis / divisor) x rate x ILF x modifiers, minimums, minus billed premium
Compare with the rating worksheet per exposure
resolution: If the recompute matches PolicyCenter (minimum premium, ILF, PCO rating), explain and close as How-to
Otherwise L3 traces the GL rate routine per exposure, corrects basis or slice data and runs a revised audit
workaround: Hold the bill and make a manual premium adjustment approved by Premium Audit.
permanent_fix: Fix the GL rate routine; add a GL audit regression pack with a direction test per basis type and per state.
escalation: PC L3 Rating & Audit if the recompute differs by more than 1% or $50; Sev 2 if more than one policy on the same class code or bills issued.
